en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Non-Proliferation, Concerning the Question on Inference.
4. The Question on the Non-existence in the World “Venerable Nāgasena, Buddhas are seen in the world; Paccekabuddhas are seen; disciples of the Tathāgata are seen;
universal monarchs (cakkavattirājāno) are seen; regional kings (padesarājāno) are seen; gods and humans are seen.”
The wealthy are seen, the destitute are seen; those who have fared well are seen, and those who have fared ill are seen;
the female gender appearing in a man is seen, and the male gender appearing in a woman is seen;
well-done and ill-done karma is seen, and beings experiencing the ripening of wholesome and unwholesome karmas are seen; there are beings in the world born from eggs.
There are beings born from water, born from moisture, and of spontaneous birth; there are beings with no feet, two-footed, four-footed, and many-footed.
There are in the world *yakkhas*, *rakkhasas*, *kumbhaṇḍas*, *asuras*, *dānavas*, *gandhabbas*, *petas*, and *pisācas*;
there are *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, *nāgas*, *supaṇṇas*, *siddhas*, and *vijjādharas*; there are elephants, horses, cattle, buffalo, camels, and donkeys.
Goats, sheep, deer, pigs, lions, tigers, leopards, bears, hyenas, jackals, and wolves; there are many kinds of birds;
there is gold, silver, pearls, gems, conch shells, stones, coral, rubies, emeralds, cat’s-eye, beryl, diamonds, crystal, black iron, copper, tin, bronze, and brass; there is linen cloth.
There is silk, cotton, hemp, flax, and wool; there is rice, paddy, barley, millet, rye, beans, wheat, mung beans, black gram, sesame, and lentils;
there are root-fragrances, heartwood-fragrances, sapwood-fragrances, bark-fragrances, leaf-fragrances, flower-fragrances, fruit-fragrances, and all kinds of fragrances;
there are grasses, creepers, shrubs, trees, medicinal herbs, forest giants, rivers, mountains, oceans, fish, and turtles—everything that exists in the world.
“Venerable sir, tell me what does not exist in the world.
“There are these three things, great king, that do not exist in the world.
Which three?”

“Whether conscious or unconscious, there is nothing in the world that is ageless and deathless; there is no permanence among conditioned phenomena; and in the ultimate sense, there is no finding of a ‘being. These, O Great King, are the three things that do not exist in the world.
“It is well, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; I accept it as you have said. This is the fourth dilemma:
On the Non-existence of Things in the World.
